title: W07a: worker binding store, generation and lifecycle
description: Implement the plugin's binding store and lifecycle: an explicit binding command in the worker or coordinator context taking a registered project key, a worker worktree and a stable Waystation actor; and a stored binding carrying binding ID and generation, local runtime and profile identity, verified host-supplied durable session or lineage identity, actual delegated-worker identity when needed, registration key and revision with pinned route and root, absolute canonical caller worktree and actor, and creation and update metadata with active or retired state. Validation refuses to infer session identity from model text, task titles, agent names or the active UI tab; a Hermes task identifier is never a Waystation task ID; separate delegated workers require distinct bindings whenever their execution context differs, and binding or dispatch is refused with an actionable diagnostic when the host cannot distinguish them reliably. A project, worktree or actor change requires an explicit rebind with no in-flight calls or active claims on the old binding, while a verified same worker reattaching after restart is a resume rather than a rebind. Implementation baseline: merged main 6276d5f / ledger closure e64d4bd, Waystation 0.6.0 on Bun 1.4.1; see docs/reconciliation-2026-09-27.md. Reuse the merged foundation and its tests. Start only after W07c verifies usable host identity and native MCP dispatch on the selected Hermes build. Consume W08b's single profile-state bridge/config-lock adapter and W08a's registry; do not build a competing persistence store or assume Python can import registry.ts. Own binding records and their state machine; registry records stay owned by W08.
acceptance: Two workers on one project connection hold distinct bindings, and two projects with identical task and actor names resolve to their own project.
A verified resume keeps the same binding, while a project, worktree or actor change without an explicit rebind is refused, including while in-flight calls or active claims reference the old binding.
Identical actor or task names in different projects are valid, while a second active binding for the same actor inside one project is refused.
An unverifiable session identity, such as a delegated worker or a compressed session without lineage, refuses binding with an actionable diagnostic instead of guessing.
Worker setup documents and exercises explicit bind, rebind and verified resume commands using the shared profile adapter; setup never grants task ownership without a successful Waystation claim.
notes: Acceptance group A12. Binding metadata is not task ownership: a successful Waystation claim is still required before code work. The plugin owns generation validity; no core access to the plugin store is introduced.
